Eighteenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica. Scientific Report. 2002 
Department of Ocean Development. Technical Publication No. 16. pp 227-272 
STUDIES ON FAUNAL DIVERSITY DURING XVIII INDIAN
EXPEDITION TO ANTARCTICA, 1998-99
AKHLAQ HUSAIN
Zoological Survey of India
218. Kaulagarh Road. Dehra Dun-248195
Abstract
The Paper deals with faunal diversity in Antarctica and Voyage route during the
XVIII Indian Expedition to Antarctica, 1998-99. It was observed that some of the seabirds,
particularly Skuas, encountered during the Expedition have also been reported from
the Indian region which is significicant zoogeographical point of view. Further, during
a brief stop over in Mauritius Island an attempt was made to stud) its fauna and
interestingly some common Indian birds were sighted there.
Introduction:
The faunal diversity of Antarctica and Southern and Indian Oceans has been
studied and reported by various participants/workers (Parulekar, 1982: Mathew, 1986:
Dhargalkar, 1988; Ingoie and Prulekar, 1987, 1990. 1993: Ingoie et al., !987;Hazra, 1994;
Arif, 1995; Chattopadhyay, 1995; Ramachandran and Balani, 1995: Verlencar et al.,
1996: Ghosh et al. 1997; Sathyakumar, 1998: Venkataraman, 1998; Mitra, 1999, Barman,
2000; Husain, in press a, b; Sanyal et al., in press), during the earlier expeditions which
is still scanty, may be due to harsh weather conditions over there.
During the present i.e. XVIII Indian Expedition to Antarctica, 1998-99 the author
had the opportunity to study various faunal groups in Schirmarcher Oasis (Antarctica),
during the voyage and at Mauritius island which are dealt here with.
SCHIRMACHER OASIS, ANTARCTICA
The Oasis is situated at about 100 km inside Princes Astrid coast of Queen
Maud Land between the ice shelf and the ice dome in Antarctica. It covers about 34 sq.
km (about 3.5 km in max. width, 20 km in length) of low lying hilly area (elevation ranging
from sea level to 228 m with an average of 100 m) located between Lat. 70°44.21'E to
70°46.04'E and Longs. 11° 26.03' Eto 11° 49.54'E. The area is oriented approximately in
east-west direction. The gentle slopes and almost plain areas are mostly covered by a 
228
Akhlaq Husain 
thin layer of moraine debris. The ice bodies surrounding the oasis are the ice shelf
about 200-500 m thick and 100 km wide in the north and rem glacier basin about 1000 m 
thick and 50 km wide between the nunateks and Wohlthat massif in the south. The
steeply inclined ice part lies between these two icy areas, terminating as 10 to 40 m high
escarpment on the southern edge of Oasis while showing a smooth transition to ice
shelf towards both east and west of the area
The extreme air temperature at Schirmarcher Oasis vary from a minimum of about
-40°Celsius (August, 1984) in winter to a maximum of about -8.5° Celsius (January,
1999) in summer. At some distance from the Oasis. the temperatures are generally less
by 5°Celsius. The precipitation (average between 250-300 mm)  is in the form of snow
fall which is quite heavy during winter months but most of it is below in the form of
blizzards by the strong Catabatic winds from easterly direction. South of the Oasis,
snow accumulation begins at 500 m above the sea level going up to the slope of the
Wohlthat massif. The relative humidity is about 50 per cent. In summer the highest
winds (40K.T) and maximum gust (60 K.T) mostly recorded were in the month of January,
1999 whereas in winter they reach at their highest (60K.T and 79K.T respectively) in the
month of October, 1998. The climatic zone of influence in the Oasis extends to about
1000 Sq. Km including the ice shelf. During summer the banks of many lakes, glacier
sides and other such moist places are thickly covered with patches of moss carpets or
turfs, mostly belonging to Bryum sp.
Maitri Area: The permanent Indian Station "Maim" is located at Lat. 70°
45.39' S, Long. 11° 44.49' E with a elevation of 10.5 m on ice free rocky area along
southern bank ofZub or Priyadarshini Lake in Schirmarcher Oasis.
